source_text: Martianus ait: Da nomina, ne poenae ipse succumbas. respondit Achatius: Ante tribunal ipse assisto, et nomen inquiris? an speras quod multos valeas vincere, quem ego solus extinguo? si cordi tuo nomina sunt, Achatius dicor, et si proprium nomen meum exploras, vocor Agathangelus, et Piso Troianorum episcopus, et Menander presbyter. fac iam quod placet. Martianus ait: Recipieris in carcerem, ut imperator gesta cognoscat et eius nutu quid de te agi debeat decernatur. lectis itaque omnibus gestis Decius imperator, alterationem iam redditae responsionis admirans, versus in risum est et Martiano praefecturam Pamphyliae mox dedit, Achatium vero vehementer admirans aestimationi propriae et legi suae reddidit. haec facta sunt a Martiano consulari, imperatore Decio, quarto kalendas Aprilis.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus says: Give the names, lest you yourself yield to punishment. Achatius answered: I myself stand before the tribunal, and do you ask for my name? Or do you hope that you are able to conquer many, when I alone extinguish you? If the names are upon your heart, I am called Achatius, and if you search out my own proper name, I am called Agathangelus, and also Piso, bishop of the Trojans, and Menander the presbyter. Do now what pleases you. Martianus says: You shall be taken back into prison, so that the emperor may learn the proceedings and by his nod it may be decided what ought to be done concerning you. Therefore when all the proceedings had been read, Decius the emperor, marveling at the sharp exchange of the answer already returned, turned into laughter and soon gave to Martianus the prefecture of Pamphylia, but admiring Achatius greatly he restored him to his own judgment and to his own law. These things were done by Martianus the consular, under Decius as emperor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.
pass_b_english: Martianus said, Give me the names, or you yourself will break under torment.
Achatius replied, I stand here in person before the tribunal, and yet you ask my name?
Do you expect to master many others, when I alone silence you?

If these names lie heavy on your heart, I am known as Achatius, and if you are hunting for my true name, I am called Agathangelus, together with Piso the bishop of the Trojans and Menander the priest.
Martianus said, You will be carried back to prison, until the emperor comes to know the acts and by his bidding it is settled what must be done with you.

So when the whole record had been read, Decius the emperor marveled at the keen exchange in the answer already given, broke into laughter, and at once bestowed on Martian the governorship of Pamphylia, while in great admiration for Achatius he set him free to his own conscience and his own law.
This was accomplished through Martianus the consular, in the reign of Decius as emperor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

choices.english: I am standing here before your own court
choices.why: ipse intensifies the speaker as subject of assisto, and ante with accusative marks place before the court, not assistance to it

choices.english: when I alone put you out
choices.why: relative quem refers back to Martianus as opponent; solus agrees with ego and stresses one man against many, with future force in the dispute
rejected: whom I alone will extinguish with fire

choices.term: aestimationi propriae et legi suae reddidit
choices.english: handed him back to his own conscience and his own law
choices.why: reddere with datives of destination signals release to his own judgment in context of admiration, not condemnation under imperial law
rejected: restored his proper value and law
